cells.tense: Right now you are taking in the pull of several possible feelings without letting any one of them claim you.
cells.ask: For one hour, notice each pull toward someone or something as it arrives, and before you follow it, let it stand on its own. Nothing gets dropped.
cells.core:
The pull is arriving whole and you're receiving it whole. Something draws you toward a person, a room, a plan, and it stays a draw — you feel how it might go without having to know yet, and the picture doesn't get scrambled by it. Nothing in you is racing the moment or hiding from it. That's rarer than it sounds.

A feeling is real on both sides of it. What you can do today is keep the weighing where it belongs: let each pull come to you by itself, and before you answer it, see whether it reads the same when it isn't carried by the one before. That's not hesitation. It's you keeping the line clear, so the one you do choose is a real choice and not this morning's noise. The ease lasts only while you keep doing that.
cells.sheetLine: You feel the pull without letting it decide for you.
cells.verb: gathering every feeling that might be had and letting the pull of it decide what comes
cells.place: where what each side owes the other gets weighed and brought back level

cells.tense: You are already bracing for the moment this reaches you, and the brace is doing the pulling.
cells.ask: When the next pull toward someone shows up, write it down and do nothing with it for the day. If it's still there tonight, follow it then.
cells.core:
You keep running to the end of something that hasn't happened. A pull toward someone or something arrives, and you're already there with it — how you'll come across, how they'll take it, what it will cost if you don't handle it right. So one good possibility turns into a quiz, and you answer the quiz the loud way because that feels like control.

The pull gets decided by whoever gets loudest first, and the loudest is usually the one that's next, not the one that matters. What you can do about it sits in the other direction: take the pull as it arrives, write it down, and let it wait a day before you act on it. Anything left by tomorrow is yours to act on. The bracing passes when it isn't being fed.
cells.sheetLine: You're deciding the pull before it has a chance to arrive.

cells.tense: What was available then went untouched, and you are still counting it as gone.
cells.ask: Open one plan with another person and leave it open. Say what you'd like, let them answer, and don't settle the shape of it before the week is out.
cells.core:
There was a stretch when possibilities were live and you didn't reach for any of them. The pull was there and your hands stayed down. Whether that was caution or something else running underneath — whatever was happening then isn't the whole of what's happening now, and more than one thing might be true about it. What's left is a thinness: few of the pulls reach you as yours, so it feels like the deciding is happening somewhere you can't get to.

Warmth hasn't gone anywhere. What's missing is a way to hold more than one open possibility at once, so you can start small with one plan and one other person. Leave room in it for them. Not settling the shape of it early is what letting the pull stay real looks like from here. That's where the earlier lack gets loosened, in an open plan with room in it.

cells.tense: You are already drawing people toward a shape of feeling the moment hasn't shown yet, and treating it as the room's own mood.
cells.ask: Say you were drawn to someone or something before they felt it, and name what you did to make it show. Do it once, to the person closest to it.
cells.core:
People are catching a feeling they didn't have before they walked in. You shift how you stand, where you put your eyes, how much of what's moving in you reaches the surface, and the pull gets felt by the room before anything has actually happened. That's not a trick, and it isn't mostly deliberate.

What you can do today is go back through one recent moment with someone and trace it from your side: what you did, when you did it, and what followed. Doing that lands it as yours instead of just the room's own mood. A feeling you can trace is one you're steering with, and one you can decide about.

A pull is a real thing between two people. What you're gathering into the space goes back out of it — once you can trace it, it stops arriving on its own.

attempts.check: The record supports a pull toward many emotional possibilities that must be chosen among; it does not support that anyone is actually offering the person those possibilities, nor who they are, so 'every yes is a real one' and similar shaping stay out. A reader could reasonably say the pull is mostly worry about how it will look, or mostly tiredness, not abundance — the ask is written so it still yields something even then, because opening a space or letting one wait costs nothing and teaches the settling either way. The sentence that served me more than them was the one about the heart's harvest arriving with their name on it across a table; it is gone.
